newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends up on small rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends up on small rate cut.

text.p: A lower-than-expected cut in the Central Bank's overnight rates helped the Philippine peso gain ground at the close on Tuesday at 26.322 from 26.329, traders said.
"The market was expecting the Central Bank's overnight borrowing rate to be slashed to ten or 10.125 percent. But it was just down to 10.25 percent," a foreign bank dealer said.
"Instead of buying up dollars, they sold," he added.
Early in the day, the Central Bank dropped its overnight borrowing and lending rates by 0.1875 percentage point each to 10.25 and 12.75 percent respectively.
The cut was triggered by the sharp fall in Treasury bill rates in Monday's auction caused by the high liquidity in the system.
Market volume, however, had thinned to $118 million from 263.30 million due to the lack of incentive to buy up the dollar, traders said.
Some inflows continued to come in, which prodded the Central Bank to buy about $20 million at 26.322, dealers said.
